turns.q:
Your response was: "Looked at it. Most of it made sense. One thing didn't — two buttons at the bottom. Went to the wrong one first. Darker one drew my eye. That wasn't the action I needed."

We want to understand what you meant by "went to the wrong one first", so let's go a bit deeper. Which of these best captures what you were pointing at?

A) The visual hierarchy is inverted, as the dark "Continue Shopping" button appears more prominent than the light "Place Order" button despite being the secondary action.
B) The vertical placement is counter-intuitive, with the secondary action ("Continue Shopping") positioned above the primary action ("Place Order").
C) The grouping of the two buttons at the bottom creates ambiguity about which one is the final step to complete the transaction.
D) None of the above — but only if A, B, and C genuinely miss what you meant (you must still name the specific element you were referring to)

Select A, B, C, or D to continue.
What was happening in your workflow when you first noticed that the Continue Shopping button drew more attention than Place Order?
